result.summary: READ-ONLY review of target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (feature/binary-config-serve-20260930), scope: dispatch pending/sending/sent/completed transitions, exactly-once/idempotent delivery boundaries, message loss/duplication, crash recovery. Verdict FINDINGS: 1 HIGH (reproduced) + 1 LOW. HIGH src/coordinator.ts:226-237: queueMessage's paused+terminal-previous_state revive branch never cancels the predecessor run, so a follow-up acknowledged as delivery:'queued' is never submitted and the worker wedges permanently in recovery_required. Reported LOW: send_worker_message has no idempotency key. Everything else in scope verified sound (atomic pending->sending claim, no duplicate submit, stable-message-ID crash resolution, duplicate-completion guard, run_id-scoped fallback). /workspace/repo left clean at baseline 5672ead; experiments only in /tmp. Artifacts: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md and findings.json.
result.details:
HIGH finding, reproduced with the repo's own fakes on Bun 1.4.2. Chain: (1) submit outcome unknown after claimDispatch committed state 'sending' (crash between claim and OpenCode ack, or connection-level promptAsync failure); step()'s catch leaves the run 'sending' because fallback() only accepts a result.json whose run_id matches the new run. (2) monitor() (coordinator.ts:568-579) finds no message with d.message_id, sees the session idle, and after SWARMFORGE_API_TIMEOUT_MS escalates to recovery_required WITHOUT cancelDispatches, so the run stays 'sending' forever. (3) The operator pauses the retained VM to inspect it, exactly what the emitted error text and docs/MCP-API.md:29 instruct; worker becomes paused with previous_state 'recovery_required'. (4) send_worker_message takes the w.state==='paused' branch at 226-237, which only patches previous_state to 'booting' and enqueues the new run; the cancelDispatches at 223 is gated on w.state being failed/recovery_required, which it is not. (5) resume -> booting -> ready; step() calls store.dispatch(id), which returns the OLDEST non-terminal run (store.ts:236-240), i.e. the stale 'sending' run, so d.state !== 'pending', the monitor branch is taken and the worker returns to recovery_required next tick.

Consequence: the run is reported as {delivery:'queued', state:'paused'} then silently never delivered (stays 'pending'; submits stays 1). The worker is permanently wedged: recovery_required is terminal, so runTick filters it (344-349) and runRecover returns early (420); no deadline, token-progress or ambiguity timer clears it. Stable after 30 ticks. Every later follow-up is accepted and also never delivered; only explicit cancel/destroy clears it. Same root cause also stalls a follow-up behind a stale 'sent' run from the destroy quiesce path (919-926).

Why guards/tests miss it: tearingDown/intent guards (201-208) cover in-flight teardown, not stale rows; 'oldest open run wins' is correct for ordering but is applied in the revive path with no check that the selected run is the one being revived; the comment at 197-200 claims no run is acknowledged as queued then silently removed, and this is the mirror case (acknowledged then stranded). tests/lifecycle.test.ts covers paused-revive only with previous_state 'completed', and recovery_required+message only WITHOUT pause (line 655); the broken combination is untested. A fix candidate validated in a throwaway /tmp test (cancelDispatches in the paused/terminal branch) makes the follow-up submit.

LOW: send_worker_message (mcp.ts:120-126, coordinator.ts:192-250) has no request_id, so a retry after a timeout enqueues a duplicate turn, unlike retry-safe spawn_worker. At-least-once by design; docs prescribe request_id only for creation.

Verified sound: single-delivery inside one process (deliver only on 'pending' + atomic claim + exclusive()/ticking guards + messageID provider idempotency key); interrupted-submit crash recovery via stable message ID with escalation instead of blind replay (ARCHITECTURE.md:24); duplicate completion/usage guards (store.ts:277-299, 307-322); run_id-scoped fallback blocking stale result files; acknowledged-but-dropped protection around fail/cancel/destroy; queue-full predicate consistent with dispatch() selection.

Limitations: no full-suite run and no compile (whole-suite/packaging scopes own those); no real provider, model endpoint or VM contacted; the post-crash 'sending' state was built via Store.saveDispatch because a real crash cannot be staged in-process; the 30s escalation timing and OpenCode messageID idempotency are code-evidenced only. Delta from baseline 5672ead in this scope is only shutdown tracking; store.ts/domain.ts/opencode.ts are unchanged, so the defect is long-standing. No credentials in any output.

tests.summary: In-scope existing tests all pass (81/81, exit 0). The reviewer probe fails exactly as the reported HIGH defect predicts (exit 1, acknowledged follow-up stays 'pending', worker wedged in recovery_required, submits stays 1) and its paired control case passes, isolating the cause to the paused-revive branch. bun test exit codes captured; no cloud or model provider contacted.

Reviewer experiments live only in /tmp: disposable detached clone /tmp/rev-d428 (git rev-parse HEAD verified = d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895) and experiment copy /tmp/probe. /workspace/repo was left unchanged and clean at baseline 5672ead.
No full-suite run and no compile/package step; bun run check was not executed. Scope was limited to dispatch delivery.

The post-crash 'sending' state in the reproduction was constructed via Store.saveDispatch because a real crash cannot be staged in-process; it is the exact persisted shape Store.claimDispatch commits.
Real-world timing of the 30s ambiguity escalation and OpenCode's messageID idempotency behaviour are code-evidenced only, not verified against a live OpenCode server or real VM.

The 'sent'-state variant of the HIGH finding (destroy quiesce path, lines 919-926) was observed with a hand-built recovery_required state rather than by driving the full destroy/quiesce sequence, so that sub-case is lower severity and partly unverified.
result.followup_reason: HIGH finding at src/coordinator.ts:226-237 (target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895): the paused+terminal-previous_state revive branch in queueMessage enqueues a follow-up without cancelling the predecessor run, so a message acknowledged with delivery:'queued' is never submitted and the worker is permanently wedged in recovery_required (reproduced; 30 ticks; control case without pause delivers correctly). Fix by cancelling non-terminal runs in that branch (or refusing when store.dispatch(id) is not the run just enqueued), and add a regression test combining a paused worker with previous_state 'recovery_required' plus a follow-up message. LOW: add an idempotency key to send_worker_message.
